title: The Transformer Architecture
description: Explore the complete Transformer architecture: Multi-Head Attention, Positional Encoding, and Encoder vs Decoder families.

slides.title: Attention Is All You Need (2017) 📜
slides.content:
# The Transformer Revolution

Published by Vaswani et al. at Google Brain/Research, the **Transformer** completely discarded recurrence and convolutions in favor of **Self-Attention**.

### The Core Innovations:
1. **Massive Parallelism:** All tokens in a sequence are processed simultaneously in parallel matrices, saturating GPUs.
2. **Positional Encoding:** Because attention is permutation-invariant, sinusoidal or rotary position embeddings (RoPE) are added to give tokens awareness of sequence order.
3. **Multi-Head Attention:** Multiple attention projections run in parallel, allowing the model to attend simultaneously to syntactic structure, pronoun resolution, and semantic themes.

slides.title: The Transformer Family Tree 🌳
slides.content:
# Encoder vs Decoder Paradigms

| Architecture Branch | Landmark Models | Attention Masking | Ideal Applications |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Encoder-Only** | BERT, RoBERTa | Bidirectional (every token sees past and future tokens) | Classification, Named Entity Recognition, Vector Search |
| **Decoder-Only** | GPT-4, LLaMA, Claude, Mistral | Causal (masked: tokens can only attend to past tokens) | Autoregressive text generation, chat assistants, code synthesis |
| **Encoder-Decoder** | T5, BART | Bidirectional encoder + Causal decoder | Translation, Abstractive summarization |

quizData.question: Why do modern autoregressive models (like GPT-4 and LLaMA) use a Causal Attention Mask in their decoder layers?

options.text: To prevent future tokens from leaking into the prediction of the current token during training
To force the model to output only lowercase text
To convert token embeddings into audio files

quizData.explanation: A causal mask sets attention scores for future positions to -infinity, ensuring the model predicts next tokens solely from previous context.

slides.title: Multi-Head Attention in PyTorch 🐍
slides.codeSnippet:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# Sequence: batch=2, seq_len=4, embed_dim=64
seq = torch.randn(2, 4, 64)

# 8 parallel attention heads (each head has dim = 64/8 = 8)
mha = nn.MultiheadAttention(embed_dim=64, num_heads=8, batch_first=True)
attn_output, attn_weights = mha(seq, seq, seq)

print('Output tensor shape: ', attn_output.shape)
print('Attention weights shape:', attn_weights.shape)
